title: Physics Mock Test №10
subtitle: 45 tasks • 55 scored items • 3 hours • with formula sheet and calculator

questions.text: The figure shows a graph of the velocity of a body versus time. Find the distance (m) travelled by the body in 12 s.

A boat is moving upstream against a current flowing at 6 m/s. If it is at rest relative to a cyclist riding along the bank against the current at 9 m/s, find the speed of the boat relative to the water (m/s).
Find the acceleration due to gravity (m/s²) at the surface of a planet whose mass is 4 times greater and whose radius is 2 times smaller than those of the Earth. g_Earth = 10 m/s².
Two bodies were thrown upward on the Moon with an initial speed of 25 m/s, 6 s apart. How many seconds after the first body was thrown will they meet? g_Moon = 5/3 m/s²
A gas passed from state A to state B as shown in the diagram. Determine the work (kJ) done by the gas against external forces.
Using the data in the diagram, determine the tension forces (N) in the strings. m₁ = 2 kg, m₂ = 5 kg, m₃ = 3 kg. T_I = ?, T_II = ?
A body sinks in kerosene with an acceleration of 4 m/s². With what acceleration (m/s²) will it sink in water? ρ_water = 1 g/cm³, ρ_kerosene = 0.8 g/cm³.

Loads of masses m₁ = 4 kg and m₂ = 6 kg are attached to the ends of a spring of stiffness 2 kN/m, as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction for each load is 0.1. Find by how many centimetres the spring stretches.
By what percentage does the period of oscillation of a simple pendulum increase when it is placed in the cabin of a high-speed elevator descending with an acceleration of 0.36g?
When an ideal gas passes from the first state to the second, its temperature changes by 330 °C. If V₁ = 3.2 m³ and V₂ = 6.4 m³, what was the initial temperature of the gas (K)?
The density of an ideal gas is 1.2 kg/m³ and its pressure is 16 kPa. What is the root-mean-square speed of the gas molecules (m/s)?
The base area of a load placed on a plane is 10 cm². If the system is moved upward at a speed of 2 m/s, what is the pressure (Pa) exerted by the load on the plane? The mass of the load is 4 kg.
Using the given graph and electric circuit, find the total charge of the circuit.

Bodies K and L are hung from a weightless rod with equal divisions, suspended at point O, and the rod remains in horizontal equilibrium. If the volume of body L is 10 cm³ and its density is 4 g/cm³, what is the mass of body K (g)? (ρ_water = 1 g/cm³)

In a magnetic field of induction 15 mT, a wire of length 25 cm and electrical resistance 0.5 Ω moves at a constant speed of 36 km/h, as shown in the figure. Find the induced current (mA) in the circuit.

An electric circuit is made of capacitors with capacitances C₁ = 6 nF, C₂ = 2 nF and C₃ = 4 nF. Capacitors C₁ and C₂ are connected in parallel, and C₃ is connected in series with them; the circuit is charged from a DC voltage source. If the charge on the first capacitor is 12 nC, find the charge on the third capacitor (nC).

After the external circuit is connected, the potential difference across the battery terminals is U = 18 V. The resistance of the external circuit is R = 6 Ω. If the emf of the battery is 30 V, find the internal resistance of the battery (Ω).

A circuit of three identical conductors connected in parallel to the mains releases a certain amount of heat in t₁ = 40 s. In what time t₂ will the same amount of heat be released if these conductors are connected in series?
A ball of mass m attached to a spring performs simple harmonic motion; 3 is the equilibrium point. At which point(s) is its energy greatest?
Find the kinetic energy (mJ) of a 2 μC charge that has passed through a potential difference of 500 V starting from rest.
While charging a bank of 20 capacitors connected in parallel, 10 J of heat was released. If the capacitance of each capacitor is 4 μF, determine the voltage across the capacitors (V).
A capacitor of capacitance 1 μF is connected to an AC circuit of frequency 50 Hz. Determine the capacitive reactance of the capacitor.
A force F = 0.15 N acts on a straight conductor of length l = 0.5 m placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of induction B = 2·10⁻² T. Find the current (A) through the conductor.
A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and disconnected from the voltage source. How does the electric field energy density in the capacitor change if the plates are moved farther apart?
If the frequency of a simple pendulum increases by a factor of 1.5 when the length of its string is shortened by 5 cm, find the initial length of the string (cm).

The primary winding of a step-down transformer with a transformation ratio of 8 is connected to a 220 V mains. The resistance of the secondary winding is 2 Ω and the current in it is 3 A. Determine the voltage (V) across the terminals of the secondary winding.

Using a converging lens, a real image of an object magnified 4 times was first obtained. Then the object was moved, and a virtual image magnified by the same factor was obtained. If the optical power of the lens is 6 D, determine the distance (m) by which the object was moved.
Two first-order maxima produced by a diffraction grating are observed at an angle of 60° to each other. How many maxima are obtained in total?
The energy of photons falling on a metal surface is 7.8·10⁻¹⁹ J, and the work function of an electron for this metal is 3·10⁻¹⁹ J. Determine the stopping voltage for the electrons (V).
Find the unknown particle in the following nuclear reaction.

What maximum kinetic energy (eV) do electrons ejected from a metal by ultraviolet radiation of wavelength 0.33 μm have? The work function of the electron is 2.8·10⁻¹⁹ J. Planck constant 6.6·10⁻³⁴ J·s. (1 eV = 1.6·10⁻¹⁹ J)
When a photon whose energy is 8/9 of the ionization energy of the hydrogen atom is absorbed, to which excited state (which level number) does the hydrogen atom go from the ground state?
Determine by how much (kJ) the internal energy of the gas changes in the transition 2 → 3 shown in the graph, if 40 kJ of heat is given to the gas.

questions.text: A body is released from rest at a height of 180 m.

parts.text: Determine the time of fall.
Determine the speed of the body 5 s after it is released.

questions.text: A spring of stiffness 1 kN/m is attached to the ceiling of an elevator, and a body of mass 10 kg is hung from it.

parts.text: By how much does the spring stretch if the system moves upward with an acceleration of 5 m/s²?
By how much is the spring deformed if the system moves downward at a speed of 5 m/s?

questions.text: Two bodies lying on a horizontal surface are connected as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction between the bodies and the surface is the same and equals 0.5.

parts.text: Determine the acceleration of the system.
Determine the tension in the string connecting the bodies.

questions.text: In an isobaric process, 40 kJ of heat is given to a monatomic ideal gas.

parts.text: Determine the change in internal energy.
Determine the work done on the gas by external forces.

questions.text: Two bodies of 5 kg each are moving in the same direction at speeds of 3 m/s and 5 m/s.

parts.text: Determine the speed of the system after the collision.
Determine the kinetic energy of the system of bodies after the collision.

questions.text: The figure shows a diagram of charged capacitors between points A and B.

parts.text: Using the diagram, determine the total capacitance. Write the answer in the form C: enter the numerical coefficient in front of C.
If the above system is connected to a DC voltage source U, determine its energy. Write the answer in the form CU²: enter the numerical coefficient in front of CU².

questions.text: A circuit is made of resistances connected in series: active resistance 5 Ω, inductive reactance 20 Ω and capacitive reactance 8 Ω.

parts.text: Find the total impedance of the circuit.
Determine what the total impedance would be if the active resistance were 0.

questions.text: A point light source is located at a distance d = 4 cm from the principal optical axis of a converging lens with focal length F = 6 cm. On the other side of the lens, a real image of the source is formed at a distance f = 12 cm from the lens.

parts.text: Determine the magnification of the lens.
Determine the distance between the light source and the lens.

questions.text: The distance between an object and its real image, magnified 3 times, is 80 cm.

parts.text: Determine the focal length of the lens.
Determine the distance from the lens to the object.

questions.text: The red limit of the photoelectric effect for the cathode material is 3·10¹⁴ Hz. Rays of frequency 6.2·10¹⁴ Hz fall on the cathode. Planck constant h = 6·10⁻³⁴ J·s.

parts.text: Determine the stopping voltage for the electrons emitted from the cathode.
Determine the momentum of the rays.
